• Merge onto **I‑278 W** (Brooklyn) → **I‑95 N** (Long Island Expressway). | | **I‑95 N through Connecticut** | 30–140 mi | • Pass through **New Haven**, **Bridgeport**, **Stamford**, **Norwalk**.
• Take exit 10 for **I‑91 S** if you need to detour to the south side of CT. | | **I‑95 N into Massachusetts** | 140–215 mi | • Continue through **New Bedford**, **Taunton**, **Fall River**.
• Enter Boston via the **Massachusetts Turnpike (I‑90 W)** at exit 1A (Boston). | | **Boston city limits** | 0–5 mi | • Follow signs for **MA‑3 N** (Massachusetts Turnpike) → **MA‑2 N** (Boston‑Cambridge Expressway) → **MA‑28 N** (North‑South Freeway) to reach downtown Boston. | **Why it’s usually fastest:** - I‑95 N is the most direct corridor between NYC and Boston. - It has multiple lanes and is designed for high‑volume traffic. - Toll plazas are minimal (only a few in Connecticut and Massachusetts). **Potential delays:** - Heavy traffic on I‑95 N during weekday rush hours (especially 7–9 am and 4–6 pm). - Construction or accidents near the Connecticut‑Massachusetts border. --- ### 2️⃣ Alternative – I‑84 W → I‑90 W (the “Turnpike” way) | Segment | Approx. distance | Key exits / landmarks | |---------|------------------|------------------------| | **NYC → I‑84 W** | 0–35 mi | • From Manhattan, take the **Brooklyn Bridge** → **I‑278 W** → **I‑95 N** → **I‑84 W** (via exit 12 in New Haven). | | **I‑84 W through Connecticut** | 35–120 mi | • Pass through **Hartford**, **Waterbury**, **Meriden**. | | **I‑84 W → I‑90 W (Massachusetts Turnpike)** | 120–215 mi | • Merge onto **I‑90 W** at exit 12 in Worcester.
• Continue on the Turnpike into Boston (exit 1A). | **Why you might choose this:** - Avoids the congested I‑95 N corridor in the mid‑section of Connecticut. - Slightly longer in mileage (~230 mi) but can be faster during peak traffic on I‑95. - The Turnpike (I‑90 W) is a toll road but offers smoother flow. --- ### 3️⃣ Quick Tips for a Smooth Trip | Tip | Why it matters | |-----|----------------| | **Check real‑time traffic** | Use Google Maps, Waze, or Apple Maps to see current congestion and suggested detours. | | **Leave early** | Aim to depart before 7 am or after 9 am to avoid the morning rush. | | **Plan for tolls** | I‑95 N has toll plazas in CT and MA; I‑90 W has tolls in MA. Consider an E‑ZPass or a prepaid toll pass. | | **Rest stops** | Major rest areas: **New Haven (I‑95)**, **Stamford (I‑95)**, **Taunton (I‑95)**, **Worcester (I‑90)**. | | **Weather alerts** | Winter storms can slow traffic dramatically; check the National Weather Service before you leave. | --- ### 4️⃣ Sample Itinerary (Assuming a 7 am Departure) | Time | Location | Action | |------|----------|--------| | 7:00 am | NYC | Start on I‑95 N via Brooklyn Bridge. | | 8:00 am | New Haven | Pass through; consider a quick stretch break. | | 9:30 am | Hartford | Continue; traffic usually light after the morning rush. | | 11:00 am | Worcester | Merge onto I‑90 W if you’re on the Turnpike route. | | 12:30 pm | Boston | Arrive in downtown Boston. | --- **Bottom line:** For most travelers, **I‑95 N** is the fastest and simplest route from New York City to Boston. If you’re traveling during peak traffic hours or want to avoid potential congestion on I‑95, consider the **I‑84 W → I‑90 W** detour. Always check live traffic updates before you hit the road. Safe travels!
